data.title: Middle East Eye: South Lebanon: 'It's torture, they are razing our lives before our eyes'
data.author: Mera Aladam
data.summary:
South Lebanon: 'It's torture, they are razing our lives before our eyes'
Day after day, the Israeli-occupied village of Mansouri, perched on a green hill a few kilometres south of the coastal city of Tyre, is slowly disappearing. Already heavily damaged during the war, it is now quite literally being wiped off the map, in a final twist of cynicism, during the ceasefire.
The Israeli army, which has made it one of its main theatres of operations for weeks, is sparing no effort: demolitions with explosives and air strikes have followed one another at a relentless pace in recent days, to the despair of the village’s roughly 5,000 inhabitants.
The village, which the Israeli army presents as an operational stronghold of Hezbollah, was initially located outside the “Yellow Line”, the “security” demarcation imposed by Israel on Lebanese territory shortly after the latest ceasefire came into effect.
Even then, residents Middle East Eye spoke to following the ceasefire feared that the zone would eventually swallow up their village. It now has, although officially only in part: the Yellow Line cuts through Mansouri, dividing it in two.
On paper, that is, as the village is now entirely occupied – this summer, all the residents who had returned to the area had no choice but to flee once again, under fire from the Israeli air force, which continues its operations.

data.author: Alex MacDonald
data.summary:
Record numbers going hungry in Yemen amid escalating conflict, WFP says
Hunger in Yemen is accelerating, with a record number of people unable to meet their food needs as conflict intensifies in the country, the World Food Programme said on Friday.
A record number of people in government-controlled areas of the country where the WFP can access are no longer able to meet their food needs, with three out of four households skipping meals, according to Matthew Hollingworth, the WFP’s assistant executive director for programme operations.
The total population of government-held areas is estimated at around 10 million people.
“The effect of this latest flare-up of insecurity on the food security situation threatens to be absolutely devastating,” Hollingworth told reporters in Geneva via video link from Rome.
Reporting by Reuters

While President Macron called Gaza 'a spectacle that shames us all', a new report reveals that France approved dozens more military exports to Israel this year
A collective of pro-Palestinian rights groups launches the "nationwide month of protest against French arms sales to Israel" on 1 October 2026 in Paris, France (Pauline Ertel/MEE)
Off
France approved 35 new sales of military equipment to Israel between May and September 2026, a new research by rights groups has found.
Jointly investigated by the Palestinian Youth Movement and the French collective Urgence Palestine, the probe documents shipments from French companies to Israel's military, including cooling systems for tanks and missile launchers, helmet visors for helicopter and fighter-jet pilots, connectors and electronic equipment, as well as surveillance systems.
"All were destined for Elbit Systems subsidiaries," the report, seen by Middle East Eye, indicates. Elbit Systems is a leading actor in the Israeli arms industry.
The findings, to be published next week, show that the equipment was manufactured across five regions in France by French companies, including the military conglomerate Thales, which produced and exported control panels used to operate weapons remotely.
These revelations come just months after the two organisations released a first joint investigation in April, which found that France exported more than 525 shipments of military-use equipment to Israel between October 2023 and March 2026.
The April report also documented 117 flights carrying F-35 fighter-jet components departing from Paris's main airport, Roissy-Charles de Gaulle (CDG).
In the new investigation, researchers identified four new suppliers and found that 33 of the 35 shipments passed through CDG airport, of which 32 were transported by Israel's national airline El Al.

Lula has warned against foreign interference in Brazil’s election, directly telling Trump in June to stay out of the contest.
According to Brazilian newspaper Folha de S.Paulo, his warning about foreign influence at the UN General Assembly also targeted Netanyahu and Argentina’s staunchly pro-Israel President Javier Milei, although he did not name them then.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Egypt detains entire newsroom of leading fact-checking platform over 'fake news' allegations
data.author: MEE staff

Reporters Without Borders denounces the arrests as the 'first' to target all staff of a media organisation, while more than 80 rights groups call for the journalists' immediate release
In this pool photograph distributed by the Russian state agency Sputnik, Egypt's President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi attends the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi on 13 September (AFP/Alexander Kazakov)
Off
Egyptian authorities have detained the entire newsroom of one of the country’s only independent media outlets in a move that rights groups have denounced as a “first” and an “alarming escalation” on free speech.
On 28 and 29 September, security forces raided the homes of the six journalists - Mohamed Ashraf Abu Emeira, Abdallah Qadry, Islam Barakat, Omar Helal, Mohamed Mahmoud and Mohamed Adel - who constitute the entire team working for Matsada2sh (Arabic for "Don’t believe").
The arrests bring the number of journalists detained in Egypt to 24.
"It is a first in Egypt: an entire newsroom behind bars," press freedom watchdog Reporters Without Borders (RSF) said, criticising the authorities for failing to reveal the journalists' whereabouts.
"It's a violation of the Egyptian Constitution, even though this is common practice. Journalists detained in Egypt are often forcibly disappeared for several days before being officially charged and brought before a court," the group added.
According to multiple accounts by rights groups, the officers confiscated the phones and laptops belonging to the journalists as well as those of their family members during the raids. They also did not present any arrest warrants and refused to disclose where the journalists would be held.

A woman soldier walks through a market in Taiz city, Taiz governorate, Yemen, 21 September 2026 (Middle East Eye)
Off
Wearing her security uniform, usually without a Kalashnikov or even a sidearm, 36-year-old Tahani walks proudly through Taiz city's markets.
While some locals remain uneasy about seeing women in military roles, others express pride and joy that Yemeni women are serving as soldiers. Female soldiers were largely absent from public view in Yemen before the war broke out in 2015.
Today, women are serving across Yemen’s security apparatus, from police stations and prosecution offices to military checkpoints and other security posts.
Tahani is one of thousands who joined the women's police force in 2022. Since then, she has served in various security offices, participating in search operations and home raids searching for criminals.
"Yemen needs female soldiers just as it needs female teachers. When I heard about the recruitment for the women's police in Taiz, I told myself that the moment had come to achieve my dream," Tahani told Middle East Eye.
Tahani, from a poor rural area, was a housewife. After getting divorced, she struggled to support her only child, making this job a vital source of income.
Every morning before heading to work, she cooks breakfast for herself and her son and prepares him for school. She then heads to the police station full of energy, ready to serve alongside her male and female colleagues.
“There are women who visit the police station almost daily, and only I or one of my female colleagues can inspect them and assist officers with their cases,” Tahani added.

Pakistan, Turkey and Saudi Arabia to hold emergency talks on Houthi attacks
Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia will top the agenda when Pakistan, Turkey and the kingdom convene emergency talks next week, Pakistani Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar says.
Speaking to reporters in Islamabad, Dar said the strategic political defence committee would meet under the three countries’ “Mecca Joint ⁠Defence Agreement”.
The countries signed the pact in August, several weeks before the Houthis began attacking the kingdom.
Dar added that more than six other countries want to join the agreement.

Teva's plant in Neot Hovav, an industrial zone south of Beersheba, Israel, on 14 December 2017 (Menahem Kahana/AFP)

The world's largest nursing union, the Royal College of Nursing (RCN), has cut ties with Israeli pharmaceutical giant Teva over its links to the country's military and a long record of corruption and bribery scandals.
Following the decision, the RCN removed Teva UK as a sponsor and partner of an upcoming event at the union's headquarters in London.
Pro-Palestine groups hailed the move as “a major breakthrough” for the international Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions (BDS) movement, which seeks to isolate Israel over the Gaza genocide and its apartheid policies in the occupied West Bank.
The RCN, which represents nearly 600,000 nurses, acted after Nurses for Palestine and UK Healthcare Petitions to Royal Colleges (UKHPRC) campaigned against the partnership.
In a public letter, nurses, midwives and healthcare professionals warned that Teva UK is “entangled with the Israeli military, part of the institutional apparatus of apartheid and responsible for corporate malfeasance”.
The letter also criticised the RCN leadership’s invocation of “political neutrality” in response to previous attempts by members to “take a clear, principled stand on the ongoing genocide in Gaza”.
“Accepting commercial sponsorship from a corporate titan deeply woven into the Israeli state’s military apparatus, and its wartime mobilisation, is the very antithesis of neutrality,” the signatories wrote.
RCN council chair Carmel O’Boyle confirmed the decision in a letter to Nurses for Palestine.

data.author: Elis Gjevori

Trump announces $8.4bn oil project under South Korea deal
US President Donald Trump says South Korea’s commitment to invest $200bn in American energy now includes an oil recovery project worth $8.4bn. The broader agreement offers Seoul lower tariffs in return for investment.
“I am thrilled to ‌announce the Republic of Korea Deal keeps getting BETTER!,” he wrote on Truth Social.
“8.4 Billion Dollars for an enhanced Oil Recovery Project. Producing more Oil and Gas means American Energy Dominance and Energy Security in the World for the ‌Future!” Trump added.
He provided no location or explanation of how the project would operate.
The announcement comes as Washington’s war on Iran disrupts oil supplies worldwide, driving up prices and leaving the US facing shortages at home.
